description: The plot illustrates how three metrics—Accuracy, Confidence, and Alignment—vary as a function of Question Popularity. The x-axis is labeled “Question Popularity,” uses a linear scale, and shows values from about 5 to 26 with major tick labels at 5-unit intervals (5, 10, 15, 20, 25). The y-axis is labeled “Values,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.55 to 1.00 with regularly spaced tick labels every 0.05. The Accuracy series is drawn as a blue solid line with circular markers, starting near 0.66 at popularity 5, dipping to about 0.60 at 6, then rising and fluctuating (around 0.75 at 8, ~0.74 at 10, ~0.81 at 12, dropping to ~0.72 at 14) before increasing to about 0.81 at 17 and ending near 0.88 at 26. The Confidence series is a green solid line with upward triangle markers, beginning around 0.93 at 5, staying in the low-to-mid 0.90s (about 0.92–0.97) with a small dip near 14 (~0.94), then increasing to roughly 0.97 at 17 and ending near 0.98 at 26. The Alignment series is a red solid line with square markers, starting around 0.73 at 5, dropping to about 0.68 at 6, then moving upward with fluctuations (about 0.75 at 6.5, ~0.80 at 9, ~0.78 at 10, peaking near ~0.86 at 12, dropping to ~0.78 at 14), then rising to about 0.84 at 17 and ending near 0.90 at 26.
